annotation.title_clean: ASTM F3269-21 Standard Practice for Methods to Safely Bound Behavior of Aircraft Systems Containing Complex Functions Using Run-Time Assurance
annotation.title_en: ASTM F3269-21 Standard Practice for Methods to Safely Bound Behavior of Aircraft Systems Containing Complex Functions Using Run-Time Assurance
annotation.venue: ASTM International Book of Standards Vol. 15.09
annotation.summary_en: ASTM F3269-21 is a voluntary standard practice giving an architectural framework for run-time assurance (RTA), which bounds the behavior of aircraft systems, especially UAS, containing complex or unassured functions such as machine-learning autopilots. It offers an alternative to design-time assurance to ease certification.
key_provisions_or_claims: Defines architecture and components of a run-time assurance system that bounds unassured complex functions.
Provides an alternative to design-time assurance for functions hard to certify under DO-178/DO-254.
Three-step process: derive RTA requirements, capture them in the larger system specification, then verify and validate.
Applies to all sizes and classes of UAS; may apply to manned aircraft and ground systems.
Appendices include examples such as GCAS, a machine-learning AI autopilot and neural-network adaptive flight control.
